title: Wendell and the Vow
premise: Ulyana Crane has spent ten years ghostwriting other people's truths, including the memoirs of her rival, the celebrated novelist Dmitri Volkov, while burying her own: a decade-old vow made to her dying mentor, Wendell, that she would never claim the orchard they restored together. When a clerical error places both her name and Dmitri's on the orchard deed, she is forced out of hiding and into a legal and emotional standoff with the one man whose success was built on a story he stole from her. As the town of Bramble Hollow rallies around her, she learns that justice sometimes arrives outside courtrooms, through testimony, loyalty, and the found family Wendell left behind. She finally speaks her rehearsed sentence, claiming both the orchard and the love she deferred, and ends the vow by rewriting the deed in her own hand.
about_author: Rafael Crane is the pen name of a former estate lawyer who traded contract disputes for love stories after a decade of watching families fight over orchards, houses, and unsaid words. They live in rural New England with a stubborn apple tree that refuses to stop bearing fruit.

chapters.title: The Ghost in the Margins
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She delivers the final chapters of Dmitri Volkov's memoirs, erasing her own fingerprints from every sentence, then retreats to her rented cottage in Bramble Hollow. The emotional beat is controlled invisibility, the comfort and quiet cost of being no one's name on a page.

chapters.title: Two Names, One Deed
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. A letter from the county clerk arrives: the orchard deed now bears both her name and Dmitri's, an impossible clerical error, or so it seems. Her hands shake as she recognizes Wendell's handwriting in the margin amendment. Beat: dread mixed with a forbidden flicker of hope.

chapters.title: What Wendell Made Us Promise
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, with a flashback chapter to the orchard's restoration years. Wendell, dying, extracted two vows: hers to stay invisible, and Dmitri's to tell the story honestly. Only one of them kept it. Beat: grief reframed as complicity; she begins to question her own loyalty.

chapters.title: The Rival Comes Home
chapters.summary: Dmitri's POV. He arrives in Bramble Hollow to contest the deed, armed with lawyers and charm, and is disarmed by the town's cold reception and by seeing Ulyana, whom he believed long gone. Beat: guilt wearing a confident mask; he knows the memoir's central story was hers.

chapters.title: Cider, Testimony, and Small Treasons
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The town's found family, Marisol the orchard keeper, old Ted the notary, Wendell's granddaughter Pim, begins quietly gathering evidence of Dmitri's theft. Ulyana and Dmitri clash over cider press and legal strategy. Beat: loyalty hardening into alliance; sparks of reluctant understanding between the two rivals.

chapters.title: The Manuscript in the Root Cellar
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Pim uncovers Wendell's root cellar cache: Ulyana's original, unpublished manuscript with Wendell's annotations proving authorship. Ulyana must choose between exposing Dmitri and protecting the decade of silence she promised. Beat: the truth becomes physical, heavy, undeniable.

chapters.title: Ten Years, One Sentence
chapters.summary: Dmitri's POV. Cornered, Dmitri confesses to Ulyana privately: he stole the story out of desperation and love he never confessed. He offers to withdraw his claim and publicly credit her. Beat: the confession she rehearsed for a decade is spoken by the wrong person, and it breaks something open in her.

chapters.title: The Hearing at the Grange Hall
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The town holds an informal hearing, justice outside the law, with testimony from Marisol, Ted, and Pim. Dmitri publicly credits Ulyana and withdraws, but the deed's amendment still names them both, and Wendell's reason emerges: he wanted them bound to the orchard, and to each other. Beat: public vindication shadowed by private confusion.

chapters.title: Frost Before Harvest
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. An early frost threatens the harvest, and Ulyana, Dmitri, and the town work through the night to save the trees, her rehearsed sentence dying on her lips as exhaustion strips away her defenses. Beat: vulnerability; love stops being past tense in the shared labor.

chapters.title: The Vow, Rewritten
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, closing with a brief Dmitri coda. At Wendell's grave beneath the oldest tree, Ulyana speaks her rehearsed sentence at last, not the renunciation she planned but a claim: of the orchard, her name, and a future she chooses with Dmitri and the family that stayed. She rewrites the deed in her own hand. Beat: resolution, harvest, and a vow finally kept by breaking it.
